lessons.title: Cats and tea
lessons.body:
## Words with kanji

Kanji often carry a reading above them, called **furigana**: {猫|ねこ} (cat), {お茶|おちゃ} (tea), {日本語|にほんご} (Japanese).

> *{猫|ねこ}が すきです。* — I like cats.

| Kanji | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {水|みず} | みず | water |
| {食|た}べる | たべる | to eat |

Katakana is for loanwords: *タクシー* (taxi), *コーヒー* (coffee).

## Pitch accent

Tokyo Japanese gives each mora (beat) of a word a high or low pitch. The line shows the high morae and the tick shows where the pitch drops. {箸|はし:1} (chopsticks) drops after its first mora; {橋|はし:2} (bridge) stays high to its end and drops before a particle: {橋|はし:2}を わたる (cross a bridge). Words with no drop are flat: [おちゃ:0] (tea). Kana words take the same marks: [ねこ:1] (cat), [タクシー:1] (taxi). The **Pitch accent** switch hides the marks.

## Writing kana

```trace
ねがパ
```

## Writing kanji

Kanji have a set stroke order too: {日|ひ} (sun, day) takes four strokes and {本|ほん} (book) five.

```trace
日本
```

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete the lesson.

questions.explanation: The verb {飲|の}みます comes last; は marks the topic and を the object. The time word {毎朝|まいあさ} can come first or after {私|わたし}は.

glossary.definition: Small kana printed above kanji to show how they're read.
